mcq_data.solution: The ternary operator returns the greater of x and y. Since 20 > 10, it prints 20.
When i == 3, 'break' exits the loop. Hence the output is 012.
Since both a and b are integers, integer division occurs first (5/2 = 2). Then it's stored in a double, so the result is 2.0.
The '==' operator compares references, not content. s1 and s2 point to different objects, so the result is false.
Dynamic method dispatch in Java ensures that the overridden method in B is executed, so it prints 'B'.
Loop prints 012, then i becomes 3 and is printed after the loop, giving 0123.
The semicolon after the for loop makes it an empty loop. After loop execution, i = 6, which is printed.
Strings are immutable in Java. concat() returns a new String but it’s not stored. So str remains 'Java'.
Array index starts at 0. arr has indexes 0,1,2. arr[3] is invalid, causing ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Static variables are shared among all objects. Changing t1.x updates it for all instances. So t2.x prints 20.
